$comment: The demo's guided tour, read top to bottom. Every field is described at the top of guide/Guide.tsx. A step without `until` waits for a click (or Space/Enter); a step with `until` waits for the visitor to do something, then moves on by itself.

steps.say: Hi there! I’m Mochiko, and I’m going to show you how Kimochi works. Click here, or press Space, to go on.
Our game today is in Japanese, but Kimochi reads lots of other languages too: Korean, Chinese, Spanish, French and many more.
Want more room? I can make the demo fill your screen. The button in the top right corner switches it back.
First, open Kimochi. Double-click its icon, up here on the left.
Everything on this little desktop is pretend, except Kimochi. That’s the real app, running right in your browser! (Well, almost: a couple of things are faked so it works here.)
Now let’s start a game. Double-click My VN.
That’s my visual novel! It’s all in Japanese, so Kimochi is going to help us read it.
Kimochi needs to know what to read. In its window, click Choose a source.
Pick Window or screen…
…and then My VN.
Now turn on Auto OCR. Kimochi will read the game every time its text changes.
Here comes a line. Watch the game!
Kimochi read it, and the line went into its Log.
To look words up in the game, turn on Show overlay.
See the boxes around the words? That’s Kimochi’s overlay.
Now let’s look a word up. Hold Shift and move your mouse over a word in the game. Try the one I’m pointing at!
Ta-da! That’s the dictionary pop-up, with the word’s reading and meanings. This one is pretend; the real one depends on the dictionary you choose.
Okay, let’s continue!
With a compatible dictionary, you can add words to Anki with the + button.
Click + now to try it!
Oh, you already added it! Nice job.
Nice! And because the Enhance Anki cards setting is on, Kimochi will detect and add the spoken dialog your computer heard for that line, as well as a screenshot.
Kimochi keeps track of the cards you make, too. Click Anki in its window.
There’s that new one you made, right at the top. You can click cards here to open 'em in Anki's browser.
(By the way click the game whenever you’re ready for the next line, just like a real visual novel.)
Oh, and now for the Notebook. This one is cool.
This is where the characters, places and words you add from the Log live. You can edit them, add pictures or notes, and Kimochi makes them clickable in the log.
Let’s see that for real; click Log to go back.
Click the one I’m pointing at to see its details in a handy lil' popup.
Pretty neat, right? You could use this to help remember the reading of a character's name. Or maybe keep track of things in a mystery game? 🕵️‍♀️
By the way, you can also add things to your Notebook directly from the Log: just select some text in a line, then right-click it.
One more trick! With Text hooking, Kimochi can read a game’s text straight out of the game, with no scanning at all. Want to see?
Text hooking works on Windows and Linux, so let’s pretend this is a Windows PC for a moment.
Open Kimochi’s source menu again.
Pick Window or screen…
…and My VN again.
Kimochi can hook this game, so there’s a Text hooking box under its card. Turn it on!
Kimochi is hooking into the game. It takes a moment the first time…
Hooked! 🪝 Kimochi found the game’s text, and each line now comes straight from the game.
Audio hooking is in the same box. With it on, your Anki cards get each line’s voice straight from the game, without the music or sound effects.
Kimochi shows each line in an overlay on the game. Right now it’s not quite in the right place. Turn on Auto align…
…and the card moves over the game’s text! Hold Shift and hover to look words up.
That’s the tour! Play around as long as you like. Kimochi is free to download.
